NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 6 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, October 18 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 13, 11:14 AM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 6 DraftKings main slate at 18.2 DraftKings points for $7,200, at the Rams. Brock Bowers (14.2, $7,500) and Isaiah Likely (12.5, $4,800) are next.

Cade Otton returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 2.65 projected points per $1,000 at $3,300.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 13, 11:14 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 6

Trey McBride, ARI at LAR ($7,200)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 18.2 DraftKings points at $7,200. That is 4.0 points clear of Brock Bowers. The model gives him 10.7 targets on 41.2 routes. The salary works out to 2.52 projected points per $1,000, 3rd of 14 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 18.1 points with a simulated floor of 6.7 and a ceiling of 37.2, and he holds 15% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 12.5-point underdog on the road against the Rams, with an implied team total of 20 in a game totaled at 52.5.

Brock Bowers, LV vs BUF ($7,500)

Brock Bowers projects 2nd at the position with 14.2 DraftKings points at $7,500. The model gives him 7.4 targets on 27.3 routes. The salary works out to 1.90 projected points per $1,000, 13th of 14 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 14.1 points with a simulated floor of 4.8 and a ceiling of 30.2, and he holds 5% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 5.5-point underdog at home against Buffalo, with an implied team total of 24 in a game totaled at 53.5.

Value: Cade Otton, TB vs PIT ($3,300)

Cade Otton projects for 8.8 DraftKings points at $3,300, which works out to 2.65 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 14 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 5.4 targets on 29.5 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Otton averaged 8.8 points with a simulated floor of 1.0 and a ceiling of 25.4, and he holds 10% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Tampa Bay is a 3-point underdog at home against Pittsburgh, with an implied team total of 18.75 in a game totaled at 40.5.
